sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test setup and fake sign-in
sections.what: Loads the test tools, replaces the sign-in check with a value the test can set, and provides a helper to create users.
sections.why: Lets each test act as a chosen user without a real login.
sections.watch_out: The fake sign-in replaces the real check for the whole file, so changes to real sign-in are not tested here.

sections.name: ROLES, entry
sections.title: Roles list and team entry builder
sections.what: Lists the eleven player roles and builds a valid team submission from the players created before the tests run.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond supplying a valid team to every test.
sections.watch_out: The entry builder relies on the setup step having run first, so running a test alone can produce an empty team.

sections.name: unique: one team per user per match
sections.title: One team per match checks
sections.what: Runs four checks: the database refuses a second team, the service returns a clear conflict, simultaneous submissions save exactly one team, and the API returns a 409 with a readable message.
sections.why: Likely reason: a duplicate would be a real bug for players, so each layer is checked.
sections.watch_out: Three parallel submissions show the common case but do not prove the code is safe under every timing.

summary: Checks that a signed-in user can submit only one fantasy team per match, and that a second attempt is refused in the database, the service and the API.
purpose: Stops a user from entering the same match twice, including when two submissions arrive at the same moment.
why: Likely reason: one team per user per match is a stated rule of the game, and the checks guard it at every layer.
how: 1) Clears the test database and creates two teams and eleven players for a match. 2) Replaces the sign-in check with a fake user. 3) Tries duplicate inserts at the database, service and API levels. 4) Sends three submissions at once and counts the teams saved.
inputs: The database through the prisma client, the test helpers in tests/helpers/db, the contest service, and the team API route.
outputs: Pass or fail for four checks on duplicates.
risks: Running these tests clears the test database, so they must never point at a live database.
debug: If the concurrency check fails, the database rule may be missing or the service may be checking before saving. If the message check fails, compare the wording in the service with the expected text.
